challenges.name: Chunk Play Club
challenges.rule: Most 40+ yard plays by your starters -- completions, runs and catches all count.
challenges.note: Actual counts are read straight from the box score. The projection multiplies each player's volume by his own measured rate of going 40+, because the feed's 40+ reception number is a placeholder -- exactly a tenth of receptions, for every receiver alive.

challenges.name: Catch Party
challenges.rule: Most combined receptions by your starting lineup.
challenges.note: Full PPR, so this is close to a points race -- but it pays volume over efficiency, which is a different team.

challenges.name: The Turnover Tax
challenges.rule: Fewest points handed back by your starters.
challenges.note: Interceptions cost 3 here rather than Yahoo's 1, a pick six costs 6, a lost fumble 2, and a missed field goal 1 or 2 by distance. Nothing under 50 yards is free. The projected column runs slightly light: Sleeper projects missed field goals only from 30-49 yards, so shorter misses appear in the actual column and in no forecast.
challenges.lineup_error: captured 2026-09-09, before week 3 began (2026-09-21 was week 2's last game) -- so it describes an earlier week than the one it is labelled with

challenges.name: Field Position
challenges.rule: Most combined kick and punt return yards by your starters, D/ST included.
challenges.note: This league pays 1 point per 20 return yards, for offensive players AND defenses. Almost no other league scores it at all, which is why this is a category worth a week.

challenges.name: The Understudy
challenges.rule: Best score from a starter you drafted in round 10 or later, or never drafted at all.
challenges.note: Keepers count at the round they cost. A waiver pickup has no round, so he counts as undrafted and is always eligible.

challenges.name: Takeaway Artist
challenges.rule: Most combined interceptions and fumble recoveries by your starting D/ST.
challenges.note: Counted as events, not points, so a defense that takes the ball away three times beats one that got there on sacks.

challenges.name: Bad Beat
challenges.rule: Score the most points and still lose your matchup.
challenges.note: Only teams that LOSE are eligible. Winners are excluded rather than ranked last.

challenges.name: Scrambled
challenges.rule: Most rushing yards from your starting quarterback.
challenges.note: A passing touchdown is worth 4 here and an interception -3, so the quarterbacks this league actually pays for are the ones who run. This is that, undiluted.

challenges.name: The Donut Shop
challenges.rule: Own the most starters who finish under five points.
challenges.note: Lands in the thick of the byes on purpose.

challenges.name: Leg Day
challenges.rule: Most fantasy points from your starting kicker.
challenges.note: Makes over 50 are worth 5 and a miss from there is free, so the winner is usually whoever's kicker plays outdoors in a bad offense.

challenges.name: One-Man Band
challenges.rule: Take the largest share of your total from a single starter.
challenges.note: A team can win this by having one enormous week or by having nine terrible ones. Both count.

challenges.name: Overachiever
challenges.rule: Beat your own lineup's projection by the most points.
challenges.note: There is nothing to project: the projected beat of a projection is zero for everybody, so this one has no projected column at all.

challenges.name: Perfect Vision
challenges.rule: Come closest to your own perfect lineup -- the highest share of the points you actually had available.
challenges.note: No luck in it at all: it scores only the decisions, against the roster you had.

challenges.name: Grand Finale
challenges.rule: Most total starting points. Last week of the regular season, no gimmick.

caveats.text: 13 of the 14 weeks have no record of who anybody actually started, so they are scored against each team's OPTIMAL lineup and labelled ASSUMED. 2 of those measure the starter/bench split itself and are placeholders until the real lineups land.

A lineup record for week 3 was refused or would not load, so that week fell back to the assumed lineup. The reason is on the week's own card. A refused record is the system working: a capture that cannot prove which week it describes is worse than none.
A projected winner is an expected value, not a forecast of the winner. Expected 40+ plays of 1.4 does not mean one happens; read the projected column as who is best positioned, not who will win.

Everything is scored in this league's own rules -- full PPR, return yards at 1 per 20, -3 interceptions, the 40+ bonus ladder, raised DST tiers -- not in Yahoo's defaults and not in any site's standard scoring. These numbers will not match other sites, and that is the point.
